solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Seed: just what's needed for bird

parts.note: a pip is a small fruit seed
'that's it' means exactly the thing required

explanation.surface: A bird-keeper notes that seed is all a bird requires.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon makes seed look like the bird's diet; really it is the first piece of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipit is a small brown songbird of open country, so it is one example of a bird.

clue.text: Never smart, supporting police force

indicators.note: in a down clue whatever supports sits underneath, so this piece goes below the others

parts.note: pigs is slang for police officers
might is strength or force
fly is British slang for sharp or streetwise

explanation.surface: Someone who is never well dressed props up the police.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' means placed underneath, so the smart piece sits below the police force pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a sarcastic reply meaning something will not happen at all, the same as saying it never will.

clue.text: Are Rovers under pressure in such a tournament?

indicators.note: in a down clue being under means placed lower in the column, so this piece follows the other

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
people who roam are rovers

explanation.surface: A football team called Rovers under pressure in some tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: Rovers looks like a club name (Blackburn Rovers, Bristol Rovers); here 'are rovers' is read as a verb, they roam. In a down clue 'under' puts it below the pressure letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pro-am is an event, typically golf, in which professional and amateur players compete together.

clue.text: Barriers the reverse of substantial, weak and small

indicators.note: the reverse of something is it run backwards, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: fat as in a fat sum, a substantial one
frail means feeble or weak
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Barriers described as the opposite of substantial: flimsy and small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The reverse of substantial' invites an antonym such as thin; it means one synonym of substantial written backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffrails are the handrails round the stern of a ship, which are safety barriers along the deck edge.

clue.text: Cosmetic to remain on cheek

parts.note: lip means impudent talk, cheek
to stick is to stay put, remain

explanation.surface: Make-up that should stay put once applied to the cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' places the remain piece after the cheek piece. Cheek reads as a face part but means impudence.
explanation.definitionFit: Lipstick is a coloured stick of make-up applied to the mouth, a standard cosmetic product.

clue.text: Keen viewer having a right to enter box used by commentators

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: the lynx is proverbial for sharp eyesight, hence lynx-eyed
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An eager spectator wants to get into the commentary box at a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The commentary box of a stadium is really the voice box, which commentators use constantly.
explanation.definitionFit: The larynx is the voice box in the throat, the organ that anyone speaking on air relies on.

clue.text: Chances are ultimately plentiful, for new arrival at the periphery

parts.note: pro is Latin for for, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: something at the periphery lies round the edge, so it wraps around another piece

parts.note: a newborn baby is a new arrival

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of plentiful

explanation.surface: The odds of plenty look good for a newcomer on the fringe.
explanation.walkthrough: The baby goes round the single letter and the Latin-derived for goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'chances are' means something is likely, which is exactly what the adverb conveys in a sentence.

clue.text: I'm obliged to weed lake

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you
to hoe is to clear weeds with a garden tool

explanation.surface: Someone feels duty-bound to clear the weeds from a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm obliged' is a polite thanks, not a statement of duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Tahoe is a large freshwater lake in the Sierra Nevada on the California–Nevada border.

clue.text: Likely person's taken unawares and worried

parts.note: a candid photo is one taken without the subject knowing
ate as in 'what's eating you?', worried

explanation.surface: The favourite has been caught off guard and is anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate is someone suitable or in the running for a post, a likely choice for selection.

clue.text: Worthless, mushy stuff, finally obtained free

parts.note: goo is sticky, soft stuff

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter of the word is used

parts.note: the final letter of obtained
free means at no cost, for nothing

explanation.surface: Someone scorns sentimental rubbish that ended up being given away.
explanation.walkthrough: Mushy stuff suggests sentimentality but is the plain sticky substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something good-for-nothing is useless and of no value, so the compound adjective is a synonym.

clue.text: City inn's watchdog barking

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, and crazy letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pub's guard dog is yapping loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking fits the watchdog perfectly, but it is the British slang for barking mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Washington, DC is the capital of the United States, one particular city.

clue.text: Notes mostly recall accompanying answer

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the tail letter is dropped

parts.note: memory, the power of recall, missing its last letter
and joins things that go together
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: Notes that mostly jog the memory come with the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: Recall is a verb in the surface but must be read as the noun memory.
explanation.definitionFit: Memoranda is the Latin plural of memorandum, written reminders or short records, i.e. notes.

clue.text: Maybe miss return of Nazi-led demos

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards
a demo shows something, so the letters are on display within the words

parts.note: inside the hyphenated word

explanation.surface: Someone might miss a comeback of fascist street marches.
explanation.walkthrough: Miss is a title here, not a verb; 'maybe' flags Eliza as just one example of a young woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliza is a girl's name, as in Miss Eliza Doolittle, so it can be an example of a miss.

clue.text: Stop seeing short, grotesque creature

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the tail letter goes

parts.note: to lose sight

explanation.surface: Stop looking at a squat, ugly monster.
explanation.walkthrough: Short looks like a description of the creature but is a deletion signal; drop the final D.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblin is a mischievous, ugly sprite of folklore, a typical grotesque being from fairy tales.

clue.text: Party recalled destiny to fight case for democracy?

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters go back the other way

parts.note: Lab is the abbreviation for the UK Labour Party
one's lot is one's fate
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A political party revisits its fate while fighting for the democratic cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case for democracy' sounds like an argument; it is a literal container. The question mark flags that wordplay on 'case'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballot box is the sealed container into which voters drop their papers at an election.

clue.text: Being hasty is blow to career

definitions.note: 'being hasty' read as a descriptive phrase, matching the adjective

parts.note: a slap is a blow with the open hand
to career is to rush headlong, dash

explanation.surface: Rushing things can damage your professional prospects.
explanation.walkthrough: Career is a noun in the surface but a verb meaning to hurtle in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash describes work done hurriedly and carelessly, which is what acting too quickly produces.

clue.text: Contribute something dramatic separately

parts.note: a play is a drama for the stage
apart means separately

explanation.surface: Each person adds something theatrical of their own.
explanation.walkthrough: The second word must be split into two to fit the enumeration.
explanation.definitionFit: To play a part in something is to have a role in it, meaning to help or add to it.

clue.text: Style of football a long time coming after defeat by English

indicators.note: arriving later in a sequence means being written further along in the entry

parts.note: a rout is a crushing defeat
an eon is an age
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A long-awaited football approach follows England's loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming after' puts the long time after the defeat, and 'by' puts English beside that.
explanation.definitionFit: Route one is British football slang for the direct long-ball game, kicking straight from defence to attack.

clue.text: Keep rabbit connected to post?

parts.note: surface reading: hold a pet bunny tied to a fence post
setter's reading: keep chattering (rabbit, from rhyming slang rabbit and pork) about your post, your job

explanation.walkthrough: Rabbit is British rhyming slang: rabbit and pork means talk. Post is a job, not a stake.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk shop is to discuss your work in company, chatting on endlessly about job matters.

clue.text: Local Tennessee state visits

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside a place, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: TN is the postal code for Tennessee
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: A native of Tennessee pays a visit to another state.
explanation.walkthrough: State looks like a US state beside Tennessee but is the verb. A local is British for one's nearby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A tavern is an inn or pub, and in Britain your regular pub is called your local.

clue.text: Mount pictures a painter's put in

indicators.note: something put in goes inside another thing, so it is placed within

parts.note: pictures collectively are art
taken as written
RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: An artist's work is mounted and framed.
explanation.walkthrough: Mount looks like a verb about framing pictures; it is the noun for a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Ararat in Turkey is the peak where Noah's Ark traditionally came to rest.

clue.text: Boy emptied ladleful round yard

indicators.note: an emptied thing has had its contents removed, leaving only the outer shell of letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of ladleful
O is round in shape
YD is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: A lad tips out a ladle's contents around the yard.
explanation.walkthrough: Round looks like it means 'around the yard' but supplies a letter shaped like a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Lloyd is a male first name, and crosswords use boy to clue any boy's name.

clue.text: Keeping low profile, Harry quit

parts.note: to dog is to pursue or harry
to go is to leave, quit

explanation.surface: Prince Harry stepped back from royal duties to stay out of the public eye.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry looks like the prince but is a verb meaning to harass.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie doggo is British slang for staying hidden and still, so doggo describes someone lying low.

clue.text: Reversal of spell after the first go?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a complete change of position or opinion
second meaning: alternation, where each person's stint follows the other's in rotation

explanation.walkthrough: Spell reads as magic, as in reversing a spell; it is a stint, and go is a turn.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a U-turn in policy and taking turns in alternation, one stint following another.

clue.text: Ancient working nurses led out

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so one piece cradles another

parts.note: a machine that is on is working

indicators.note: out means disordered or not in place, so the letters get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly working woman tends patients, who are led outside.
explanation.walkthrough: Nurses reads as a noun, the people; it is the verb meaning to hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Olden is a poetic adjective for bygone times, as in the olden days, so it means very old.

clue.text: What big, year-round op sorted out

indicators.note: sorting out puts things into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A large all-year operation that has been dealt with.
explanation.walkthrough: The one-word definition is the exclamation 'What?' asking someone to repeat themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are polite or blunt requests to repeat something not heard, used interchangeably in speech.

clue.text: One demonstrating skill and power

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a practitioner or champion of an art
second meaning: the index in mathematics

explanation.walkthrough: Power reads as strength beside skill, but it is the mathematical sense, as in ten to the power of three.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a skilled practitioner of something and the superscript index in algebra.

clue.text: VAT is charged primarily for clothing

parts.note: a vat and a tun are both large casks

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letters of the words are kept

parts.note: the first letters of is and charged

explanation.surface: Value added tax is levied on garments.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT looks like the British sales tax; it is a big container for liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunic is a loose garment reaching the hips or knees, one kind of clothing item.
